fields.index_subject_description: Woman in her80s with T2DM/DPN, osteoporosis/L1 compression fracture and physical frailty
fields.care_setting: Hospital outpatient rehabilitation under Japan’s long-term care insurance
fields.chief_complaint: Residual weight loss, reduced mobility and poor glycemic control after hospitalization

evidence.quote: The patient in this case was a woman in her 80s with T2DM (height: 154.0 cm, weight: 36.6 kg, body mass index: 15.4 kg/m^(2), level of care: support needed 2) who used the OR facility covered by Japan’s long-term care insurance system. The complications included DPN, osteoporosis, and a compression fracture of the first lumbar vertebra. Ten months before starting OR, the patient sustained a first lumbar compression fracture and was diagnosed with T2DM at the time of injury. Subsequently, rapid weight loss of approximately 10 kg and poor glycemic control continued over 4 months, resulting in a 1-month educational admission to our hospital. The patient remained hyperglycemic even after discharge and was readmitted to the hospital for glycemic control; however, during this hospitalization, the patient was advised bed rest for COVID-19. Consequently, the patient was discharged from the hospital with residual weight loss, reduced mobility, and poor glycemic control, and started OR at the hospital.

evidence.quote: This report suggests that long-term continuation of OR may contribute to improvements in KEF, physical frailty, and glycemic control in a frail older patient with T2DM.

The patient in this case was a woman in her 80s with T2DM (height: 154.0 cm, weight: 36.6 kg, body mass index: 15.4 kg/m^(2), level of care: support needed 2) who used the OR facility covered by Japan’s long-term care insurance system. The complications included DPN, osteoporosis, and a compression fracture of the first lumbar vertebra. Ten months before starting OR, the patient sustained a first lumbar compression fracture and was diagnosed with T2DM at the time of injury. Subsequently, rapid weight loss of approximately 10 kg and poor glycemic control continued over 4 months, resulting in a 1-month educational admission to our hospital. The patient remained hyperglycemic even after discharge and was readmitted to the hospital for glycemic control; however, during this hospitalization, the patient was advised bed rest for COVID-19. Consequently, the patient was discharged from the hospital with residual weight loss, reduced mobility, and poor glycemic control, and started OR at the hospital.

summary.text: A woman in her 80s with T2DM diagnosed at an L1 compression fracture 10 months before rehabilitation, DPN and osteoporosis lost approximately 10 kg over four months. She underwent a one-month educational admission, then readmission for persistent hyperglycemia with COVID-19 bed-rest advice. After discharge she entered rehabilitation with residual weight loss, reduced mobility and poor glycemic control. Baseline weight was36.6 kg, BMI15.4 kg/m², HbA1c9.1%, HOMA beta-cell function2.57%, and four J-CHS frailty criteria were present, with reduced knee and grip strength.

Two years of outpatient rehabilitation provided80-minute sessions twice weekly, with individualized, self-directed and seated/group exercise, safety supports, low-to-moderate intensity, home walking/resistance guidance and increased food intake. Only two sessions were missed because of weather. SMBG changed to FreeStyle Libre isCGM around month9 and Libre2 from month18, with glucose/TIR/TBR feedback. Tresiba changed from8 to10 units/day at month3 and back to8 at month6, then to Novolin R8 units/day at month12 and Tresiba8 from month14. Glimepiride stopped at month8 and mitiglinide increased to three daily doses at month11. Insulin ingredients and routes remain unreported.

J-CHS classification changed from frail at baseline to pre-frail at months3/6 and robust at months9/12/24. At two years, right/left knee extension forces were26.4/23.5 kgf, grip strengths22.5/20 kg, weight45 kg, GNRI94, chair stands19, TUG8.45 s, six-minute walk365 m and LSA59.5 points. She ate out and shopped with friends/family by month9 and flew with family by month21. HbA1c remained below baseline despite worsening at months9–12; two-year HbA1c was7.8%, with better second-year control. TBR was0% after isCGM and severe hypoglycemia did not occur. Proposed muscle recovery and lifestyle/season contributions remain qualified author interpretations.
